name: ossify
description: Skeleton-first lifecycle from Release 0 through MVP and v1. workspace-init is optional: /ossify:start and /ossify:adopt author .ossify/topology.json themselves. Grill/critic ship as /ossify:challenge. /ossify:start onboards, /ossify:adopt takes on an existing repo, /ossify:plan-release and /ossify:plan-spine plan, /ossify:run-spine drives rounds, /ossify:close closes, /ossify:doctor diagnoses, /ossify:wayfinder charts tickets, /ossify:patch ships a shipped defect or a small can't-fake request as a versioned patch, plus the any-repo /ossify:handoff and /ossify:work-pr. Since 1.8.0 /ossify:run-spine accepts an optional --external-executor flag that hands a round's work items to a caller-supplied, provider-neutral in-session procedure; the no-flag command is unchanged. Since 1.14.0 /ossify:run-spine re-enters a started spine on its own, at a round barrier or mid-round, printing a reconcile read-out and halting before any mutation on state it cannot reconcile. Since 1.26.0 `--external-executor --detach` ends the lane after it writes a round's requests and leaves counting, close and merge to the caller; `/close <wi-id> --pr` opens the item's PR; re-entry reads an item with a recorded PR as in flight. Since 1.16.0 a demo line starts planned until its spine builds it, and a spine's own user line can be deferred to a release or closed under a declared escape. Since 1.17.0 an AC can name both halves (`exit <n> and output contains <str>`), an output check never passes a command that cannot run, and every prose snippet calls `oss` by name. Since 1.28.0 work-item close runs its pattern, lens and mutation checks in a fresh verifier subagent.
